p.seg: First Meeting with the Chief Minister of Qín
Your servant has heard it said:
"To speak without knowing
is unwise;
to know and not speak
is disloyal."
To be a disloyal minister
deserves death;
to speak improperly
also deserves death.
Nevertheless,
your servant wishes to fully state what he has heard,
may the Great King judge his crime.
Your servant has heard:
The world covertly aligns Yān and overtly aligns Wèi,
unites Jīng (Chǔ) and secures Qí,
gathers Hán to form an alliance,
intending to face west to create difficulties for the powerful Qín.
Your servant secretly laughs at this.
There are three ways to ruin oneself,
and the world has embraced them.
Is this what it means!
Your servant has heard it said:
"To attack order with chaos leads to ruin,
"To attack righteousness with wickedness leads to destruction;
to attack obedience with rebellion leads to destruction."
Today, the treasuries of the world are not full,
and the granaries are empty.
Exhausting all their soldiers and people,
deploying armies numbering in the hundreds of thousands,
and appointing generals who bow their heads and wear feathers,
those who choose to die at the front
do not even reach a thousand.
They all die speaking (giving reasons).
With sharp blades in front,
and axes and chisels behind,
they retreat and cannot die.
It is not that the soldiers and people are unable to die,
but that their superiors are unable to make it happen.
When rewards are promised, they are not given;
when punishments are announced, they are not carried out.
Rewards and punishments are not credible,
therefore, the soldiers and people do not die.
Now, when Qín issues commands and carries out rewards and punishments,
the meritorious and the unmeritorious attend to their duties.
Emerging from the bosom of their parents,
they have never seen an enemy in their lives.
Upon hearing of battle,
they stamp their feet, bare their arms,
Facing naked blades,
treading on hot coals,
those who resolutely die in the front lines
are all examples of this.
Now, resolute death is different from resolute survival,
yet the people do it,
which shows they value fighting to the death.
One man fighting to the death can take on ten,
ten can take on a hundred,
a hundred can take on a thousand,
a thousand can take on ten thousand,
and ten thousand can conquer the world.
Now, the land of Qín, after adjusting for its unevenness,
is several thousand *lǐ* square,
and has hundreds of thousands of famous soldiers.
As for Qín's commands, rewards, punishments,
terrain advantages, and disadvantages,
no one in the world is better.
With this, Qín fights against the world,
and the world is not enough to be completely conquered.
Therefore, Qín's battles have never failed to be victorious,
its attacks have never failed to capture,
and whatever it faced has never failed to be destroyed.
It has opened up thousands of *lǐ* of land;
this is its great achievement.
However, the armor and weapons were blunted,
the soldiers and people suffered,
the reserves were exhausted,
the fields lay waste,
the granaries were empty,
the neighboring lords did not submit,
and the name of a hegemon could not be established.
There is no other reason for this,
it is because the strategists did not all exert their loyalty.
I dare to speak of it.
In the past, Qí attacked Jīng in the south,
attacked Sòng in the east,
subdued Qín in the west,
and attacked Yàn in the north.
It used Hán and
Wèi as its envoys in the middle,
its territory was vast and its army was strong,
winning battles and taking territory,
and its edicts commanded the world.
The clear Jì River and the muddy Hé River of Qí
were enough to serve as borders;
the long walls and great defenses
were enough to serve as fortresses.
Qí,
was a state that could be destroyed by five battles;
One battle does not subdue and there is no Qí [齊].
From this perspective,
warfare is
a matter of survival for a state with ten thousand chariots.
Moreover, I have heard it said:
"Cut away the stump, leaving no root,
have nothing to do with the neighbor of misfortune,
then misfortune will not exist."
Qín [秦] fought against the Jīng [荊] people,
greatly defeating Jīng [荊],
and raided Yǐng [郢],
seizing Dòngtíng [洞庭],
Wǔzhǔ [五渚],
and Jiāngnán [江南].
The Jīng [荊] king and his ministers fled,
submitting to Chén [陳] in the east.
At this time,
if we had pursued Jīng [荊] with our army,
then Jīng [荊] could have been conquered;
if Jīng [荊] could have been conquered,
then its people would have been worth coveting,
its land worth exploiting,
in the east we could have weakened Qí [齊] and Yàn [燕],
and in the center we could have dominated the Three Jìn [三晉].
However, in that case, with one action,
the reputation of a hegemon and king could be established,
and the surrounding feudal lords could come to court;
yet the strategist did not act accordingly,
but led the army to retreat,
and once again made peace with the people of Jīng.
Allowing the people of Jīng to recover their lost state,
gather their scattered people,
establish a lord of the state and altars of the soil and grain,
and set up ancestral temples;
causing them to lead the world westward
to make trouble for Qín.
This indeed is the first loss of the way of a hegemon and king.
The world then formed alliances and mustered their armies below Mount Huá,
the Great King used an edict to defeat them,
and the army arrived below the walls of Liáng.
Besieging Liáng for several weeks,
then Liáng could be captured;
capturing Liáng,
then Wèi could be taken;
taking Wèi,
then the intentions of Jīng and
Zhào would be severed;
the intentions of Jīng and Zhào being severed,
then Zhào would be in danger;
Zhào was in danger, and Jīng was hesitant;
to the east, they could weaken Qí and
Yān,
and in the center, they could dominate the Three Jìn states.
In that case, with one move, the name of hegemony could be achieved,
and the neighboring lords could come to court.
Yet the strategists did not act,
but withdrew the troops,
and instead made peace with the Wèi clan.
This allowed the Wèi clan to reclaim lost territory,
gather dispersed people,
establish a ruler of the state,
set up ancestral temples,
and lead the world to face west and make trouble for Qín.
This is certainly the second way in which they have lost the path to hegemony.
Previously, when Rǎng Hóu governed Qín,
he used the troops of one state
to achieve the merits of two states.
Therefore, the soldiers were exposed abroad year-round,
and the soldiers and people were exhausted within,
and the name of hegemony was not achieved.
This is certainly the third way in which they have lost the path to hegemony.
The Zhào clan
is a state in the center,
inhabited by mixed people,
Its people are frivolous and difficult to employ.
Commands and orders are not effective,
rewards and punishments are not trusted,
the terrain is unfavorable,
and superiors cannot fully utilize the strength of their people.
This is certainly the form of a country destined for destruction,
yet they do not worry about the people,
but mobilize all their soldiers and people to the area below Chángpíng 長平,
to contend for Hán 韓's Shàngdǎng 上黨.
Your Majesty used imperial edicts to defeat them,
and captured Wǔ'ān 武安.
At that time,
the Zhao 趙 family's upper and lower ranks were not close to each other,
and the noble and the base did not trust each other.
In that case, Hándān 邯鄲 cannot be defended.
Capture Hándān 邯鄲,
control the area east of the mountains and Héjiān 河間,
withdraw the army,
attack Xiūwǔ 脩武 to the west,
cross the Yángcháng 羊腸,
and subdue Dài 代 and
Shàngdǎng 上黨.
All thirty-six counties of Dài 代,
and seventeen counties of Shàngdǎng 上黨,
can be obtained without using a single suit of armor,
Not even bothering a single commoner,
all these territories already belong to Qín 秦.
Dài 代 and Shàngdǎng 上黨 completely fell to Qín 秦 without a fight.
Dōngyáng 東陽 and
the area north of the Yellow River (Héwài 河外) completely revolted and joined Qí 齊 without a fight.
Zhōngshān 中山 and
the region north of the Hūtuó 呼沱 River completely fell to Yān 燕 without a fight.
If this is what Zhào 趙 does,
and Zhào 趙 succeeds, then Hán 韓 will perish.
If Hán 韓 perishes, then Jīng 荊 (Chǔ 楚) and
Wèi 魏 cannot stand alone.
If Jīng 荊 (Chǔ 楚) and Wèi 魏 cannot stand alone,
then with a single action, we will destroy Hán 韓,
weaken Wèi 魏,
and control Jīng 荊 (Chǔ 楚).
To the east, we will weaken Qí 齊 and Yān 燕.
By opening the mouth of the Bái mǎ 白馬 Canal to flood the lands of the Wèi 魏 clan,
with this single action, the Three Jìn 三晉 states will be destroyed,
and those who follow them will be defeated.
If Your Majesty simply sits back and waits,
the world will fall into line and submit,
and the reputation of a hegemon or king can be established.
But instead, our strategists did not do this,
but withdrew the army,
and resumed peace with the Zhào 趙 clan.
Now, with the King's (dàwáng's) perspicacity,
and the Qin army's strength,
to abandon the enterprise of hegemony,
territory once not unattainable,
to instead be deceived by a destroyed state,
is the clumsiness of a strategist.
Moreover, Zhao, when it ought to have perished, did not perish,
and Qin, when it ought to have achieved hegemony, did not achieve hegemony.
The world surely had already measured the strategists of Qin as one (fault).
Then to again exhaust all soldiers to attack Hándān,
and fail to conquer it,
discarding armor, weapons, and crossbows,
trembling in battle and retreating,
the world surely had already measured the strength of Qin as two (faults).
The army then withdrew and retreated,
uniting at Lǐxià.
The King (dàwáng) again united the army and arrived,
and fighting, was unable to overcome them,
and again unable to reverse the situation,
the army wearily departed.
The world surely had already measured the strength of Qin as three (faults).
Internally, they measure our strategists;
externally, they exhaust our military strength.
Judging from this,
I, your subject, believe that gaining the allegiance of the world
is not so difficult.
Internally,
our armor and weapons are blunted,
our soldiers and people are weary,
our reserves are depleted,
our fields lie fallow,
and our granaries are empty.
Externally,
the world is united and their intentions are very firm.
I hope Your Majesty will give this some thought.
Moreover, I have heard it said:
"Be ever cautious and trembling,
be more careful each day."
If one is cautious in their way,
the world can be possessed.
How do I know this is true?
In the past, Zhòu 紂 was the Son of Heaven,
leading a million soldiers and armor-bearers,
drinking on the left at the Qíxī 淇溪,
and drinking on the right at the Huánxī 洹溪,
so that the Qí River 淇水 was drained and the Huán River 洹水 did not flow,
in order to make things difficult for King Wǔ of Zhōu 周武王.
King Wǔ 武王, leading three thousand soldiers in plain armor,
fought for one day
and destroyed Zhòu's 紂 state,
captured him,
seized his land, and possessed his people,
and the world suffered no harm.
With this to control the world,
it can all be possessed.
Your servant, braving death, desires to see Your Majesty,
to speak of the means to break the alliance of the world,
to conquer Zhào,
destroy Hán,
make Chǔ and Wèi subjects,
befriend Qí and Yān,
in order to achieve the name of a hegemon king,
and cause the neighboring lords to come to court.
If Your Majesty truly listens to his plan,
and with one action the alliance of the world is not broken,
Zhào is not conquered,
Hán is not destroyed,
Chǔ and Wèi do not become subjects,
Qí and Yān do not become friends,
the name of a hegemon king is not achieved,
the neighboring lords do not come to court,
then Your Majesty should execute me and display my head to the country,
as a warning to those who give disloyal advice to the king.
Preserving Hán, part two.
Hán has served Qín for over thirty years,
going out to act as a shield,
When they enter, they become mats and cushions.
Qín especially sent out elite troops to seize territory
and Hán followed behind them,
resentment was directed at them by all under Heaven,
while the credit went to the powerful Qín.
Moreover, Hán entering with tributary duties
is no different from a commandery and county.
Now, I have secretly heard of your esteemed ministers' plan
to raise troops and attack Hán.
Now, the Zhào family gathers soldiers,
supports followers,
wanting to attach the troops of all under Heaven,
making clear that Qín is not weak,
then the feudal lords will surely destroy their ancestral temples,
wanting to face west and carry out their intentions,
this is not a plan of one day.
Now, releasing the troubles of Zhào,
and expelling the internal subject, Hán,
then all under Heaven will understand the plan of the Zhào family.
Now, Hán
is a small country,
and uses this to respond to attacks from all directions under Heaven,
the ruler is humiliated, and the ministers suffer,
those above and below have shared the same worries for a long time.
They cultivate their defenses,
Be wary of powerful enemies,
have accumulated resources,
build city walls
to defend them securely.
Now, to attack Hán,
it cannot be destroyed in a year.
If we seize one city and retreat,
then our power will be seen as light in the world,
and the world will defeat our army.
If Hán rebels,
then Wèi will respond to it,
and Zhào will rely on Qí for support.
If this happens,
then Hàn and
Wèi will provide resources to Zhào, who will borrow power from Qí,
to strengthen their alliance,
and use it to compete with us for power.
This will be a blessing for Zhào and a disaster for Qín.
Moreover, if we advance and attack Zhào but cannot take it,
and retreat to attack Hán but cannot conquer it,
then the elite troops will be exhausted in field battles,
and those burdened with the task will be weary from internal sieges.
Thus, combining weak forces to oppose
two ten-thousand-chariot states together is
not the way to achieve the intention of destroying Hán.
If we follow the esteemed minister's plan,
Then Qín 秦 will surely become the hostage of the world's armies.
Even if Your Majesty exhausts [resources] with gold and metal [in war],
the day of unifying the world will still be distant.
Now, this foolish subject's humble plan:
Send someone as an envoy to Jīng 荊,
heavily bribe the influential ministers,
and make clear to them the reasons why Zhào 趙 deceived Qín 秦;
send a hostage to Wèi 魏 to reassure them,
follow Hàn 韓 and attack Zhào 趙.
Even if Zhào 趙 unites with Qí 齊,
it is not worth worrying about.
After the affairs of these two states are concluded,
then Hàn 韓 can be settled with a letter.
This way, with one move, two states will be on the verge of destruction,
then Jīng 荊 and
Wèi 魏 will surely submit themselves.
Therefore, it is said:
"War is an ominous tool."
It is imperative to use it prudently.
If Qín 秦 and Zhào 趙 are equally matched
and balanced,
and Qí 齊 is added,
now you turn your back on Hàn 韓,
and you have not yet solidified the hearts of Jīng 荊 and
The heart of Wei.
Now, if one battle is not won,
then disaster will befall us.
Planning
is that by which affairs are decided,
and cannot be overlooked.
The strength or weakness of Zhao and Qin
lies in this year.
Moreover, Zhao has been secretly plotting with the various lords for a long time.
Now, to act in a way that makes us weaker than the other lords
is a dangerous thing;
to plan in a way that makes the other lords suspicious of us
is extremely perilous.
To show two sources of distrust
is not a way to become stronger than the other lords.
Your servant humbly hopes that Your Majesty will carefully consider this!
To attack and subjugate, allowing the followers of others to intercede,
cannot be undone.
The decree concerns the memorial presented by the Han guest,
the memorial stating that Hán Zǐ is not yet to be elevated,
and has been sent down to your servant, Sī.
Your servant, Sī, strongly believes this is not so.
Qin's possession of Han
is like a man with a disease in his heart and abdomen.
An empty place is humid,
like a place that is damp,
sticking and not leaving,
which, if extremely rushed,
will erupt.
Now, although Hán is a subject of Qín,
it has never not been a problem for Qín.
Now, if there should be an unexpected urgent matter,
Hán cannot be trusted.
Qín and Zhào are in difficulty,
Jīng Sū has been sent to Qí,
it is not yet known how it will turn out.
From my perspective,
the alliance of Qí,
and Zhào
will not necessarily be broken because of Jīng Sū.
If it is not broken,
it means facing Qín with the strength of two states with ten thousand chariots each.
Now, Hán does not submit to Qín because of righteousness
but submits because of its strength.
Now, if they focus on Qí
and Zhào,
then Hán will surely become a disease in the heart
and erupt.
If Hán conspires with Jīng,
and the other lords respond,
Then Qin will certainly see again the calamities of the Xiao Pass.
As for Fēi's coming,
it is not necessarily that his ability to preserve Hàn
is not more important to him than Hàn itself.
He uses eloquent arguments and fine phrases,
covering up falsehoods with deceitful schemes,
to fish for benefits from Qin,
while using Hàn's advantages to spy on Your Majesty.
If the relationship between Qin and Hàn
becomes close,
then Fēi will gain importance,
this is a plan that benefits him alone.
I see Fēi's words as
elegant, but his persuasive arguments are dissolute and confusing,
his talent is excessive.
I fear that Your Majesty will be seduced by Fēi's eloquence
and listen to his thieving heart,
and consequently not carefully examine the situation.
Now, according to my humble opinion:
Qin has sent out troops but has not specified the target of the attack,
then Hàn's officials will certainly see serving Qin as their main strategy.
I, Sī, request to go and meet the King of Hàn,
to have him come and present himself;
when Your Majesty sees him,
keep him and do not send him back,
Slightly summon its ministers of state (responsible for land and grain),
to engage in trade with the people of Hán,
then Hán can be deeply divided.
Then order Xiàng Wǔ to dispatch troops from Dōngjùn,
to observe the troops on the border
without declaring their destination,
then the people of Qí will fear
and follow Sū's plan.
Thus, our troops have not yet been deployed
yet a strong Hán will be captured through coercion,
and a powerful Qí will be persuaded through righteousness.
When this is heard by the feudal lords,
the Zhào clan will be frightened,
the Jīng people will be suspicious and hesitant,
and they will surely come up with loyal strategies.
If the Jīng people do not act,
Wèi is not worth worrying about,
then the feudal lords can be gradually devoured,
and the Zhào clan can be fought against.
I hope Your Majesty will carefully consider your humble servant's plan,
and not disregard it.
Qín then sent Sī as an envoy to Hán.
Lǐ Sī went to inform the King of Hán,
but was unable to see him,
so he submitted a memorial, saying:
"In the past, Qín and Hán united their strength and purpose
to not invade each other.
The world dared not offend them.
This continued for several generations.
Previously, five feudal lords once joined together to attack Hán.
Qín sent troops to rescue them.
Hán is situated in the central plains.
Its territory is not even a thousand *lǐ*.
The reason it has been able to maintain its position among the feudal lords in the world,
with its ruler and ministers secure,
is because for generations they have taught each other
to dedicate their strength to serving Qín.
Before this, when five feudal lords jointly attacked Qín,
Hán instead led the other feudal lords like a wild goose formation,
to guide the troops to attack the Qín army below the pass.
The feudal lords' soldiers were exhausted and their strength depleted.
Having no other choice,
the feudal lords' troops retreated.
Dù Cāng was the chancellor of Qín.
He raised troops and sent generals to avenge the grievances of the world
and first attacked Jīng.
The Prime Minister of Jīng was troubled by this
and said:
'Hán considers Qín to be unjust,
and yet it acts as a brother to Qín,
causing suffering to the world together.
Hàn had already betrayed Qín again,
first forming a goose formation to attack the passes.
Hán then resided in the central region,
making their movements unpredictable."
The world together ceded ten cities of Hàn's upper territory
to apologize to Qín,
and to have them withdraw their troops.
"Hán once betrayed Qín
and their state was pressed, their land invaded,
and their military weak to this day.
The reason for this is
they listened to the superficial words of treacherous ministers,
and did not weigh the actual facts.
Therefore, even though they killed the treacherous ministers,
they could not make Hán strong again."
"Now Zhào desires to gather soldiers
and treat Qín as their objective,
sending people to request passage,
claiming they want to attack Qín.
In reality, they will attack Hán first and then Qín.
Moreover, I have heard it said:
'If the lips are gone,
the teeth will be cold.'
Qín and
Hán cannot help but share the same anxieties;
Its form is visible.
Wèi wanted to send troops to attack Hán,
Qín sent someone to lead an envoy to Hán.
Now the King of Qín has sent his minister Sī to come,
but he cannot be received.
I fear that those around you are following the schemes of past treacherous ministers,
causing Hán to once again suffer the misfortune of lost territory.
If your minister Sī cannot be received,
I request to return and report,
and the relationship between Qín and Hán will surely be severed.
The reason Sī came as an envoy
was to serve the pleasure of the King of Qín,
willing to offer convenient plans.
Is this how Your Majesty treats lowly ministers?
Your minister Sī wishes to be granted an audience,
to advance and speak of my foolish plans,
and retreat to be diced into mincemeat.
I hope Your Majesty will give it some thought.
If you kill your minister in Hán now,
then the Great King will not become stronger.
If you do not listen to your minister's plan,
then disaster will surely arise.
If Qín sends troops without delay,
then the altars of Hán will be in danger.
If your minister Sī exposes his body in the marketplace of Hán,
Then even if you wanted to discern the foolishly loyal plans of your lowly servant,
it would be impossible.
If the borders are ravaged,
and the state holds firm to its defenses,
with the sound of drums and bells in your ears,
and only then you employ the plans of Chén Sī,
it will be too late.
Moreover, the state of Hán's military strength is known to all under Heaven,
and now it has also turned its back on the powerful Qín.
If cities are abandoned and armies defeated,
then the brigands of Fǎnyè will surely attack the cities.
If the cities are all lost, then the people will scatter;
if the people scatter, then there will be no army.
If the cities hold firm,
then Qín will surely raise an army and besiege your capital;
if the roads are blocked,
then difficulties will inevitably arise,
and the situation will be beyond salvation.
If those advising you on the left and right are not heeded,
I hope Your Majesty will consider this carefully.
If what Chén Sī has said does not accord with the facts,
I hope Your Majesty will be so kind as to allow me to finish my words before you,
and then it would not be too late to hand me over to the officials for punishment.
The King of Qín (Qín Wáng) finds no savor in his food,
takes no joy in his travels and sights,
his mind solely focused on plotting against Zhào (Zhào).
He sent his envoy Sī (Sī) to say
that he wishes to meet you in person,
because he has urgent plans to discuss with Your Majesty.
If the envoy is not allowed to pass through,
then the trustworthiness of Hán (Hán) is unknowable.
For Qín (Qín) will surely release its worries about Zhào (Zhào)
and shift its troops to Hán (Hán).
I hope Your Majesty will carefully reconsider the plan,
and grant me a reply and decision."
"The Difficulty of Speaking," Section Three
It is not that I am unwilling to speak;
the reason it is difficult to speak is this:
If one speaks smoothly and eloquently,
flowing and continuous,
then one will be seen as flowery but insubstantial;
if one is earnest, respectful,
direct, firm, cautious, and complete,
then one will be seen as clumsy and inept;
if one speaks voluminously, citing extensively,
drawing connections and making comparisons,
then one will be seen as empty and useless;
if one summarizes subtly and speaks concisely,
If one's path is direct and economical but not adorned,
then they will be seen as critical and sharp (劌, guì) and one will not be defended.
If one is rash and intimately close,
probing and knowing human feelings,
then they will be seen as slanderous (譖, zèn) and one will not yield.
If one is grand, vast, and extensive,
wonderfully profound and unfathomable,
then they will be seen as boastful and useless.
If one discusses domestic economy in brief,
using complete and concise words,
then they will be seen as crude.
If one's words are close to the present age,
and the language is not rebellious,
then they will be seen as greedy for life and flattering superiors.
If one's words are far from the customs of the world,
and disturb the human realm,
then they will be seen as preposterous.
If one is quick, clever, and eloquent,
abundant in literary embellishment,
then they will be seen as a mere historian.
If one abandons literary exposition,
and speaks with genuine nature,
then they will be seen as vulgar.
If one often praises the *Classic of Poetry* 《詩》(*Shī*) and the *Classic of Documents* 《書》(*Shū*),
and follows the ways of the past,
then they will be regarded as mere reciters.
This is not the reason why your servant finds it difficult to speak
and considers it a serious worry.
Therefore, even if measurements are correct,
they may not be heeded;
even if the principles of righteousness are complete,
they may not be applied.
If Your Majesty does not believe in this,
then the minor consequence will be that I am regarded as engaged in criticism and slander,
the major consequence will be trouble, misfortune, disaster, death, befalling my person.
Thus, Zǐ Xū was good at strategizing, but Wú had him executed;
Zhòngní was good at persuading, but Kuāng besieged him;
Guǎn Yíwú was truly wise, but Lǔ imprisoned him.
Therefore, these three great officials,
were they not wise?
But their three rulers were unenlightened.
In ancient times there was Tāng,
the most sage;
Yī Yǐn,
the most wise.
Now, the most wise persuaded the most sage,
yet even then, he made seventy attempts to persuade him without being accepted.
He personally held the cauldrons and cutting boards, acting as a cook,
closely associating and becoming familiar,
and only then did Tāng barely come to recognize his worth and employ him.
Therefore, it is said:
"If one uses supreme wisdom to advise a supreme sage,
one may not necessarily succeed and be accepted.
Yī Yǐn's persuasion of Tāng is an example of this.

hence those on the left and right will conceal matters for them.
If scholars are not relied upon,
then their stipends will be meager and their gifts humble,
hence scholars will speak on their behalf.
These four aids
are how wicked ministers adorn themselves.
If powerful ministers cannot be loyal to the ruler
but instead promote their enemies,
and if the ruler cannot bypass these four aids
and keenly scrutinizes his ministers,
therefore the ruler becomes increasingly obstructed
and the great ministers become increasingly powerful.
Generally, those in positions of influence near the ruler
rarely fail to be trusted and loved,
and are also accustomed to old practices.
As for those who cater to the ruler's mind,
aligning themselves with his likes and dislikes,
it is naturally how they advance themselves.
Their official positions and ranks are high and esteemed,
their cliques and factions are numerous,
and the entire state speaks up on their behalf.
Therefore, the practitioners of law and statecraft
who wish to approach the ruler,
have neither the intimacy of being trusted and loved,
nor the benefits of being accustomed to old practices;
moreover, they will use the language of law and statecraft
to correct the ruler's biased and deviant mind,
which is to oppose the ruler.
They are in humble and lowly positions,
without a party, solitary and unique.
Now, for the distant and estranged to compete with the near, beloved, and trusted,
their chances of winning are slim;
for the newly arrived to compete with the accustomed and old,
their chances of winning are slim;
for those who oppose the ruler's will
to compete with those who share his likes and dislikes,
their chances of winning are slim;
for the lowly and unimportant to compete with the high and esteemed,
their chances of winning are slim;
If one is versed in laws and methods but opposes the ruler,
if they are not executed by the officials,
they will certainly die by private swords.
Those who form factions and cliques to harm the ruler,
and those whose words are twisted to benefit their own interests,
will certainly be trusted by important people.
Therefore, those whose achievements can be used to advance themselves are elevated with official positions and ranks;
those whose fine reputation cannot be used for personal gain,
are given authority over external affairs to increase their importance.
Thus, those who harm the ruler and flock to private households,
if they do not become prominent in official positions and ranks,
will certainly have great power externally.
Now, if the ruler does not combine investigation and verification before carrying out executions,
and does not wait to see merit before bestowing ranks and emoluments,
how can scholars of law and method
be willing to risk death to present their arguments?
How can treacherous and wicked ministers be willing to take advantage of benefits and then withdraw themselves?
Therefore, the ruler becomes increasingly humble,
and private households become increasingly respected.
Although Yuè's 越 state is wealthy and its army strong,
the rulers of the Central States all know that it is of no benefit to them,
saying:
"It is not something I can control."
Nowadays, those who possess a state,
even though the land is vast and the people are numerous,
if the ruler is obstructed and ignorant,
and the high officials monopolize power,
then this state is like Yuè.
Wisdom is not similar to Yuè,
but not being wise is not similar to the state,
one does not examine its similarity.
The reason people say Qí was destroyed
is not that the land and cities were lost.
The Lǚ family could not control it,
and the Tián family employed it;
The reason people say Jìn was destroyed
is also not that the land and cities were lost.
The Jī family did not control it,
and the Six Ministers monopolized it.
Now, if high officials hold power and make decisions alone,
and the ruler does not know how to take it back,
it shows the ruler is not wise.
One who has the same illness as a dead person
cannot be brought back to life;
one who does the same things as a destroyed state
cannot survive.
Now, if you follow the paths of Qí (齊) and Jìn (晉),
desiring the state to be secure and to exist,
it is impossible.
The difficulty of implementing law and technique
is not unique to a ruler of ten thousand chariots;
it is also true for a ruler of one thousand chariots.
The attendants of the ruler need not be intelligent.
If the ruler finds someone intelligent and listens to him,
and then discusses his words with his attendants,
it is like discussing wisdom with fools.
The attendants of the ruler need not be virtuous.
If the ruler finds someone virtuous and treats him with courtesy,
and then discusses his actions with his attendants,
it is like discussing virtue with the unworthy.
When the wise make decisions based on fools,
and the virtuous measure their actions by the unworthy,
then the wise and virtuous will feel ashamed, and the ruler's discussions will be misguided.
Of the subjects who desire to obtain office,
those who cultivate themselves will fortify their persons with purity and integrity,
and those who are wise will advance their careers with skillful argument and eloquence.
Those who cultivate themselves cannot serve others through bribery,
relying on their purity and integrity,
Moreover, one must not govern by perverting the law.
Then, those who cultivate wisdom (xiū zhì zhī shì) will not serve those around the ruler,
and will not listen to requests and solicitations.
If those around the ruler (rén zhǔ zhī zuǒ yòu),
whose conduct is not like that of Bó Yí,
cannot obtain what they seek,
and bribes do not arrive,
then the effect of careful discernment will cease,
and slanderous words of defamation will arise.
If the effect of discerning arguments
is controlled by close attendants,
and the determination of pure and upright conduct
depends on praise and blame,
then officials who cultivate wisdom are cast aside,
and the ruler's discernment is blocked.
If one does not decide intelligence and conduct based on merit and achievements,
nor assess offenses through comparison and verification,
but listens to the words of those around the ruler and close attendants,
then incapable men will be in court,
and foolish and corrupt officials will hold office.
The worry of a ruler of ten thousand chariots
is that the great ministers are too powerful;
the worry of a ruler of a thousand chariots
is that he trusts those around him too much:
This is what rulers universally worry about.
Moreover, ministers have great offenses,
and rulers have great failings.
The interests of ministers and rulers are different from each other.
How can this be made clear?
It is said:
The ruler's benefit lies in having capable men and assigning them to office;
the minister's benefit lies in being incompetent and obtaining employment.
The ruler's benefit lies in having those who labor being rewarded with titles and emoluments;
the minister's benefit lies in being without merit and becoming wealthy and noble.
The ruler's benefit lies in having heroes and outstanding individuals exert their abilities;
the minister's benefit lies in forming factions and using personal connections.
Therefore, the state's territory is diminished, while private families become rich;
the ruler is demeaned, while the ministers become powerful.
Thus, the ruler loses power while the ministers gain control of the state;
the ruler is renamed a vassal,
while the chancellor divides the authority.
This is how ministers deceive the ruler and benefit themselves.
Therefore, among the powerful ministers of the current age,
those who can adapt to changes in circumstances
and maintain their secure favor
are rarely more than two or three out of ten.
What is the reason for this?
A minister's greatest crime is this:
when a minister commits a great crime,
it is that his actions deceive his ruler.
His crime deserves death.
Wise men have foresight
and fear death,
so they will certainly not follow powerful men.
Virtuous men cultivate integrity
and are ashamed to collude with treacherous ministers to deceive their ruler,
so they will certainly not follow powerful ministers.
Those who are followers of the powerful court officials (Dāngtúzhě),
if they are not foolish and unaware of trouble,
are certainly corrupt and do not avoid treachery.
Great ministers harbor foolish and corrupt men,
above, colluding with them to deceive the ruler,
below, collaborating with them to reap profits and exploit the people,
forming cliques and factions,
speaking with one voice,
confusing the ruler and undermining the law,
in order to throw the officers and people into chaos,
causing the state to be endangered and weakened,
and the ruler to be burdened and humiliated—
this is a great crime.
If a minister commits a great crime and the ruler does not prohibit it,
This is a great loss.
To cause the ruler to have great faults above,
and the ministers to have great crimes below,
to seek a state that will not perish,
is impossible.
Chapter Twelve: The Difficulty of Persuasion
Generally, the difficulty of persuasion:
It is not the difficulty of having knowledge with which to persuade,
nor is it the difficulty of being able to clearly express my intent with eloquence,
nor is it the difficulty of daring to risk failure in order to exhaust my efforts.
Generally, the difficulty of persuasion:
lies in knowing the heart of the person being persuaded,
so that my persuasion can be appropriate for him.
If the person being persuaded aims for high reputation,
and you persuade him with great profit,
then he will see you as having low principles and treating him as base,
and will certainly reject and distance himself from you.
If the person being persuaded aims for great profit,
and you persuade him with high reputation,
then he will see you as without sincerity and distant from practical matters,
and will certainly not accept you.
If the person being persuaded secretly aims for great profit
but outwardly aims for high reputation,
To persuade them with the lure of high reputation,
then Yáng would ostensibly embrace their person
but in reality keep them at a distance.
To persuade them with the promise of great profit,
then Yīn would utilize their words while conspicuously discarding their person.
These are things that must be observed carefully.
Affairs are accomplished through secrecy,
words are ruined by exposure.
It is not necessarily that they themselves divulge the secrets,
but if the conversation touches upon concealed matters,
in this way, one's person is in danger.
If they openly disclose something,
but actually accomplish something else through it,
the persuader not only knows what was disclosed,
but also knows the reason behind it,
in this way, one's person is in danger.
If one proposes an unusual plan and it succeeds,
and those who know the situation deduce it from external clues,
if the matter is leaked externally,
they will certainly think it was oneself
in this way, one's person is in danger.
If favors have not yet been deeply bestowed,
yet one speaks with extreme knowledge,
if one's advice is followed and brings success,
Then virtue is forgotten;
if your advice is not followed and results in failure,
then you will be suspected,
in such cases, one's person is in danger.
If a noble person has faults,
and the advisor openly speaks of propriety and righteousness to point out their wickedness,
in such cases, one's person is in danger.
If a noble person happens to obtain a plan and wishes to take the credit for himself,
and the advisor was involved in knowing it,
in such cases, one's person is in danger.
Forcing them to do what they cannot do,
and stopping them from doing what they cannot stop,
in such cases, one's person is in danger.
Therefore, if you discuss great men with them,
they will think you are alienating them;
if you discuss petty men with them,
they will think you are selling yourself for importance.
If you discuss what they love,
they will think you are borrowing resources;
if you discuss what they hate,
they will think you are testing them.
If you are concise in your advice,
they will think you are unwise and clumsy;
if you argue broadly about trivial matters,
Otherwise, they will consider it excessive and prolonged.
If one speaks briefly, presenting the intention concisely,
they will say you are timid and not thorough.
If one considers matters extensively and comprehensively,
they will say you are rustic and arrogant.
These difficulties in persuasion
must be understood.
In all endeavors of persuasion,
the key lies in knowing how to embellish what the person being persuaded values
and diminish what they are ashamed of.
If they have a private concern,
you must present it as a matter of public justice
and urge them on with that.
If their intentions are humble,
yet they cannot stop themselves,
the persuader should embellish its merits
and minimize the things they have not done.
If their ambition is high,
but their abilities cannot reach it,
the persuader should point out their faults
and reveal their shortcomings,
and emphasize the many things they have not accomplished.
If they desire to boast of their intelligence,
then present them with similar, but different matters,
Gain as much territory as possible;
cause them to rely on me for advice;
and feign ignorance
to fuel their wisdom.
If you want to introduce words of mutual preservation,
you must clearly state them with fine names,
and subtly show how they align with private interests.
If you want to present matters of harm and danger,
then make their slander and defamation evident
and subtly show how they align with private concerns.
Praise extraordinary people who share your path,
and plan extraordinary events with those who share your schemes.
If someone is involved in the same wrongdoing,
then you must greatly embellish it, making it seem harmless;
if someone shares in the same failure,
then you must clearly embellish it, making it seem without fault.
If they are confident in their strength,
then do not summarize the matter with its difficulties;
if they are bold in their decisions,
then do not anger them with blame;
if they are confident in their plans,
then do not drive them to ruin with their failures.
Ensure that the overall meaning does not contradict or confuse,
and that the wording is free from constraint or hindrance,
and then give full rein to your wisdom and eloquence.
This is the way to obtain [success]:
gain close proximity and trust
to fully express your opinions.
Yī Yǐn being a cook,
and Bǎi Lǐxī being a captive,
were both means to approach their superiors.
These two men
were both sages.
Yet they still had to humble themselves to advance;
that is how debased it was.
Now, if my words are treated like those of a cook or captive,
and can be heeded and employed to revitalize the world,
this is not something that one capable of serving should be ashamed of.
If one delays and distances oneself for a long time,
and the favor from above is already abundant,
deeply considering [the situation] without suspicion,
and drawing out arguments without being punished,
then one can clearly delineate advantages and disadvantages to achieve success,
and directly point out right and wrong to improve oneself.
Holding on to this principle,
this is how persuasion is achieved.
In the past, Zhèng Wǔgōng wanted to attack Hú,
so he first married his daughter to the ruler of Hú to please him.
Yīn wèn yú qúnchén:
I wish to use military force.
Who is it permissible to attack?"
The grand officer Guān Qísī replied, "
Hú is permissible to attack."
Duke Wǔ became angry and executed him,
saying, "
Hú
is a brother state.
You speak of attacking it,
why is that?"
The ruler of Hú heard of this
and considered Zhèng to be friendly towards him,
and consequently did not prepare against Zhèng.
The people of Zhèng attacked Hú
and seized it.
In Sòng there was a rich man;
it rained and his wall collapsed.
His son said, "
If it is not rebuilt,
surely there will be thieves."
The father of his neighbor also said this.
In the evening, he indeed lost much of his wealth.
His family greatly considered his son wise,
but suspected the father of his neighbor.
These two people's advice was both correct,
but the one who was straightforward was executed,
while the one who was indirect was suspected.
Therefore, it is not difficult to know
but to apply knowledge is difficult.
